gate_verdict: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. The season-controlled split-half correlation of 0.1085 sits INSIDE its permutation null band [-0.1501, 0.1272], so per-agent decision value in the running game is not a repeatable property of the agent. The board may render and be sorted by attempt VOLUME, which is a style axis; the plus metric is WITHHELD, exactly as leverage_board does today.

headline.sentence: Over eight seasons the league steals second almost exactly at its break-even. Steals of third pay, steals of home do not, and the running game costs the league 0.39 wins.

attempt_census.note: a steal attempt reaches the corpus in one of two places. A steal in the middle of a plate appearance is a row in the events table; a steal that ENDS the plate appearance, such as a caught stealing for the third out, is only the play's own result. Both are read, and a play result that is also an event row of the same type in the same plate appearance is counted once. Every attempt is either priced or counted in the exclusion table, and priced_plus_excluded equal to total is the check that says so.

running_game.attempt_census_sentence: The corpus holds 26,555 steal attempts over eight seasons: 24,036 as events inside a plate appearance, 2,519 only as the result that ended one (such as a caught stealing for the third out). 14,178 are priced and 12,377 excluded in the table above, so every attempt is one or the other.

decomposition.dv: the DECISION, priced with the league-average success rate for that season and target base.
decomposition.er: the EXECUTION RESIDUAL, realized minus expected. Attributed to the runner, never to the manager.
decomposition.identity: DV + ER = the realized win-probability change, exactly

running_game.why_two_out_attempts_are_excluded: with nobody out or one out a caught stealing leaves the inning alive, so both sides of the comparison come from the same monotone model. With two out it ends the inning, so the alternative comes from the measured half-inning-start table instead, and nothing calibrates the two estimators against each other. Across three builds of the engine that mismatch priced between 8.7% and 19.2% of attempts so that being CAUGHT STEALING HELPED the batting team, carrying up to 22.6% of the total decision value. Those attempts are excluded and counted. Pricing them needs an inning-level model that predicts the boundary and the mid-inning state together, which has not been built.
running_game.why_the_league_average_runner: the decision is scored as though the manager had a league-average runner, because the runner's speed is a roster fact and crediting a manager for having a fast team is the confound this module exists to avoid.
running_game.which_breakeven_predicts_the_sign: the swing-weighted one. DV for an attempt is (WE_success minus WE_fail) times (league_p minus p*), so the summed decision value for a group is positive exactly when the league success rate beats the swing-weighted mean of p*. The median and the plain mean are published because they are the readable summaries, and neither determines the verdict.
running_game.third_out_handling: a caught stealing with two down ends the half-inning, and the resulting state is valued as the NEXT half-inning from the other team's point of view. Pricing it as two-outs-bases-empty would understate the cost of the worst possible time to be thrown out.
running_game.why_execution_residual_does_not_sum_to_z: ER is priced against the group's OWN mean success rate, so successes and failures balance in count but need not balance in value: sum ER equals the sum over attempts of (success minus league_p) times the win-probability swing, an identity this artifact checks. RESOLVED 2026-09-06. On the full population the swing on failed attempts ran about 1.5 times the swing on successful ones, which invited a behavioural reading (defences hold runners better when it matters). It was MECHANICAL. Once the two-out attempts are excluded, and with them every caught stealing that ends an inning, the ratio falls to 1.00 on steals of second and 1.05 on steals of third. The asymmetry was the third out, not the defence. Whatever residual remains is small enough that the execution term now nearly sums to zero, which is what it should do when it is priced against its own group's mean.

gate.verdict: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. The season-controlled split-half correlation of 0.1085 sits INSIDE its permutation null band [-0.1501, 0.1272], so per-agent decision value in the running game is not a repeatable property of the agent. The board may render and be sorted by attempt VOLUME, which is a style axis; the plus metric is WITHHELD, exactly as leverage_board does today.
gate.detection_floor_reading: the smallest true per-agent per-attempt effect this battery would have detected at 80 percent power. A null without this number is unbounded and says nothing; with it, the null is a ceiling.
gate.why_the_raw_number_is_not_the_finding: Raw split-half 0.7673: both halves of an agent-season sit in the same season, so a league-wide year effect reads as agreement. Season explains 78.7 percent of the variance in a club-season's summed decision value, the club 2.1 percent. Controlled for season: 0.1085, inside its permutation band.
gate.null_construction: decision value permuted WITHIN season, holding every agent-season's attempt count and every season mean fixed. A null that reassigns attempt counts destroys the structure under test and yields a band anything clears.
gate.why_season_controlled: both halves of an agent-season sit in the same season, so a league-wide year effect reads as split-half agreement while saying nothing about the agent. A prior design note guessed the driver was target mix; that guess was wrong and the correlation between an agent's summed decision value and its share of steals of second is near zero.
gate.what_a_null_decides: a team-season is an UPPER BOUND on a manager: managers change and teams do not. If a team-season carries no repeatable decision signal in this family, fetching the manager entity to attribute that signal is not worth building FOR THIS FAMILY. It says nothing about the bullpen or the pinch hit, which have more room and have not been measured.

half_inning_start.note: P(the team coming to bat wins) at the START of each half-inning, MEASURED rather than modelled. A decision that ends a half-inning is valued from this table, not from the smooth model, because a smooth model is free to be discontinuous across a boundary it was never constrained at: two successive fits left about 8% of two-out states where making the third out RAISED the batting team's win probability. A half-inning always starts with nobody out and nobody on, so this table needs no extrapolation and its cells hold a median of 1,262 observations each. The lead is read BEFORE the leadoff play, so no cell describes a state that cannot occur.

calibration.feed_note: the MLB feed's own wp_home_before, scored on the same plays, for comparison. Measured on this build it is 0.157516 against this model's 0.157678, so the feed is very slightly ahead on Brier, by 0.00016, which is what an estimator that knows the teams should manage. That is not a ranking of win-probability models: the feed is a live in-game number solving a different problem, and the gap either way is smaller than the rounding a reader sees. What it settles is that insisting on a team-blind valuation costs nothing measurable here, which is the only question this module needed answered. The feed is still not the engine, because its within-cell standard deviation of 0.04 means it carries team quality, and crediting a manager for having better players is the confound this module exists to avoid. Both figures are derived from this fit; neither is typed.

reference.why_a_model_not_a_table: a table of cell means at this resolution cannot support differencing. Measured on the first build: advancing a runner from first to second LOWERED the batting team's win expectancy in 42.6% of comparable cells, because 1.45 million plays over 4,557 cells is about 318 each, the standard error of a binary outcome at that count is 0.029, and the effect being measured is 0.02 to 0.05. The feed's own numbers averaged the same way violate it in 24.6%.
reference.monotone_by_construction: the base-out state enters ONLY through its run expectancy, as a single covariate with a positive coefficient, so advancing a runner always raises the batting team's win probability. That property is what makes differencing safe and it is asserted in the tests, not assumed.
reference.smoothing_costs_the_tails: the model is less sharp than the raw cell means at the extremes. Bottom of the ninth tied, bases empty reads 0.6396 / 0.5757 / 0.5285 by outs against published values near 0.63 / 0.57 / 0.52: the leadoff cell is about 1.0 points high, the one-out cell is about 0.6 points high and the two-out cell is about 0.8 points high. That is the price of a functional form smooth enough to difference, and it is a price worth paying, because a table that is right on average and non-monotone in the base state cannot value a decision at all. Any family reading the ninth-inning tail should say so. These three figures are interpolated from the fit this artifact ships and cannot drift from it.
reference.state_excludes: the teams, the batter, the pitcher, the park and the count. Every one matters to a real win probability and every one would let a manager's roster leak into his grade. This is a league-average valuation of a SITUATION, which is the only thing a decision can be fairly scored against.

teams.columns_are_style_not_skill: attempts, success rate and target mix are what a club chose to do; they repeat because running is a policy. Summed decision value is withheld.

chain_break.note: wpa_home equals wp_home_after minus wp_home_before on every play, every game starts at 50.0 and ends at 0.0 or 100.0, and consecutive plays do not chain on the published share of plays at the published tolerance; so a window is valued as an endpoint difference, never a row sum.

pitching_change.label: Pitching changes
pitching_change.window_rule: from the plate appearance the reliever enters to the last one he pitches: the next pitching change for that side, or the end of the game
pitching_change.counterfactual_sentence: The pitcher not used is not observed. Pricing him needs the availability model and the per-plate-appearance model, neither built, so this family carries realized value only.
pitching_change.within_family_windows: partition of each side's plate appearances once the starter's stint is included; the decision windows alone leave the starter's stint out

inherited_runners.derivation: derived: the corpus carries no per-runner scoring id, so each inherited runner is tracked through on_first / on_second / on_third across the half-inning's later plays and counted as scored on the play where his id leaves the bases while runs_scored_on_play covers him, lead runner first; a runner who leaves with no run while the half continues was out, and a pinch runner continues the man he replaced.

pitching_change.mid_pa_note: null until the corpus rebuild lands the count at the action (Wave B); the window starts at the plays row

pinch_hit.label: Pinch hitters
pinch_hit.counterfactual_sentence: The batter not lifted is not observed. Pricing him needs the per-plate-appearance model, not built, so this family carries realized value only.

pinch_run.label: Pinch runners
pinch_run.window_rule: from the plate appearance at entry to the last play of the half-inning
pinch_run.counterfactual_sentence: The runner not replaced is not observed. Pricing him needs the steal model and sprint speed, so this family carries realized value only.

defensive_sub.label: Defensive subs
defensive_sub.window_rule: from the plate appearance at entry to the end of the game; stored on each decision and never summed into a leaderboard
defensive_sub.counterfactual_sentence: The glove not used is not observed, and the rest-of-game window is dominated by everything but the glove, so this family ships timing and usage only; its window value is stored and never summed.

intentional_walk.label: Intentional walks
intentional_walk.window_rule: the walk plus the on-deck plate appearance, or the half's last play if it ends sooner
intentional_walk.counterfactual_sentence: Pitching to the batter is not observed. The state-matched league baseline is measured over the hitters a manager was willing to face, so it is biased for the walk; stated, not solved.

bunt.label: Bunts
bunt.counterfactual_sentence: The swing not taken is priced league-wide per state as the bunt DV (mgmt_bunt.py), a different quantity from the realized figure beside it; the bunt sign is not observable and the attempt is a proxy.
bunt.sign_note: the bunt sign is not observable; an attempt with a runner on and fewer than two outs is the closest proxy and is flagged sign_proxy

steal.label: Steals
steal.window_rule: the steal itself: the state before the attempt to the state after it, on the house win expectancy table (management.py); the feed carries no win probability between plays, so the steal has no play window
steal.counterfactual_sentence: The hold is priced with a league-average runner as the steal DV (management.py). The realized figure is the model's realized change of the steal itself (DV + ER), not the feed's plate appearance, whose win probability is measured after the steal and leaves it out.

realized_source.mwpa: realized_delta (management.py: DV + ER), the steal itself
realized_source.why_not_the_feed: the steal happens between two plays; the feed's plate-appearance row starts after it, so its endpoint difference is the batter's result with the steal left out

mound_visit.label: Mound visits
mound_visit.counterfactual_sentence: Counted, never valued: a visit governs no play of its own.

decisions.realized_sentence: Realized value, not skill. Each figure is the win probability that actually moved after the decision, credited to the club that made it, from the decision to the last play it governed. What the alternative would have produced, the reliever not used, the batter not lifted, the pitch not thrown, is not observed, so this is a record of what happened after a manager acted and not a measure of how well he chose. A reliever who pitched well after a poor choice and a hitter who homered after a bad matchup are both in these numbers.
decisions.agent_sentence: The agent is the club-season until the manager ledger lands; a club that changed managers during a season is one row here and two in reality.
decisions.style_sentence: Style, not skill: each is a signed z-score across the thirty club-seasons of its season, sign as measured. Not an index, no ladder, no plus sign; a frequency has no good direction, and these repeat because they are policy.
decisions.single_pa_caveat: For the single-plate-appearance families (pinch hit, bunt) the league baseline is the mean realized change over every plate appearance from the same state, which a calibrated win model puts near zero, so value above state there is the realized figure plus the feed model's local miscalibration and is not an independent second number. It differs materially only for the stint-length windows (pitching change, pinch run, intentional walk). The steal has no value above state: its realized figure is the steal itself, and its value above holding is its DV.
decisions.overlap_note: No cross-family total exists on any row. The family windows overlap: a club's intentional-walk window sits inside its own reliever's stint window, a pinch-hit plate appearance can contain that club's bunt or steal, and a pinch-run window overlaps the pinch hit before it, so one composite per club-season would double count. Per-family sums only.
decisions.dvs_note: Value above state removes the level of the state, so a club that faced many high-leverage spots is not credited for the spots. It does not remove player quality or selection (the manager chooses when to act), so it is realized value above what the league realized from the same spot: still descriptive, still not skill. It lives on the drill-down and the League census only, never on a club-season or manager row.
decisions.li_note: Leverage is a cut and a style axis, never a weight in the value column: a high-leverage state already moves win probability more by itself, so multiplying by leverage would count it twice.

units.mwpa: wins, realized value, not skill (wp percentage points divided by 100; the steal's is the house win expectancy change of the steal itself)
units.dvs: wins above state, realized, selection not removed
units.li: leverage index, MLB feed basis; null on the leadoff plate appearance
units.z: signed style z-score, not an index, not skill

removed_pitcher.derivation: derived: the events table carries replaced_player_id on about one pitching change in a hundred, and on a double switch that field names the lineup-slot occupant leaving, not the pitcher. The removed pitcher is the pitcher of the most recent plate appearance for the same fielding side before the change (or, when the previous change for that side sits at the same plate appearance, that change's entering pitcher); the derivation is checked against the description's replaces-NAME clause on every row and against the field on the rows whose description says replacing pitcher NAME.

ground_truth.coverage_note: ground truth exists for 2026 only, so this checks one season of eight. The other seasons rest on internal consistency (thirty clubs per season at a plausible game count), not on an external label.

baseline.identity: within every cell the residuals of the league windows sum to zero by construction; identity_max_abs is the largest absolute mean residual found, checked not asserted
baseline.single_pa_caveat: for the single-plate-appearance families (pinch hit, bunt) the baseline is the league mean realized change over every plate appearance from the same state, which a calibrated win model puts near zero, so DVS there is mWPA plus the feed model's local miscalibration and is NOT an independent second number; it differs materially only for the stint-length windows (pitching change, pinch run, intentional walk). The steal has no DVS.

selection_caveat.intentional_walk: intentional walks are given to the hitters a manager least wants to face, so the state-matched mean of pitching to him is measured over weaker batters and is biased FOR the walk. Stated, not solved.
selection_caveat.pinch_hit: a pinch hitter is sent up for the batters a manager least wants at the plate, so the state-matched league plate appearance is a different population of hitters from the ones lifted. Stated, not solved.

baseline.where_dvs_lives: the per-decision drill-down and the League census only; never a column on a club-season or manager row

clubs.style_sentence: Style, not skill: each is a signed z-score across the thirty club-seasons of its season, sign as measured. Not an index, no ladder, no plus sign; a frequency has no good direction, and these repeat because they are policy.
clubs.sort_by_realized_is_a_rank_by_what_happe: sorting a realized column ranks club-seasons by what happened after their decisions, not by how well they chose

managers.why: there is no manager entity anywhere on disk: no manager in any game feed, no manager transaction, no coach or staff cache. The ledger needs /api/v1/teams/{id}/coaches per team-season with schedule-date bisection, which is a network ingest. Until it runs every row is a club-season.

fixture.note: the ejection rows that name a manager with an mlbam id are the manager ingest's validation fixture, not a source

managers.agent_sentence: The agent is the club-season until the manager ledger lands; a club that changed managers during a season is one row here and two in reality.

challenges.blocked_on: mgmt_feeds_2026 (Wave B): the reviewDetails reader over .cache/game_feeds
challenges.why: the corpus dropped about.hasReview and carries no challenging side; the 2026 game feeds carry reviewDetails on the reviewed play and are read in Wave B. Pre-2026 side attribution is not sourceable offline.
challenges.regime_note: ABS pitch challenges (reviewType MJ, a player's challenge) are a separate 2026 regime, counted per club as abs_challenges and never mixed with replay challenges; crew-chief reviews (N*) are counted, not credited
challenges.value_not_observable: the feed prices only the final ruling, so a challenge's win-probability value is not observable even in 2026; the family ships counts, overturn rate, timing and LI

lineups.blocked_on: mgmt_feeds_2026 (Wave B): boxscore battingOrder and lineup_captures readers
lineups.why: game feeds with a batting order exist for 2026 only and are read in Wave B; pre-2026 lineups need a network fetch (M-CORPUS-2)
lineups.value_not_measured: lineup value is not measured; optimality needs the per-plate-appearance model (M-ENG-1) and the lineup chain (M-ENG-2), neither built

shards.schema_note: schema 2: one array per decision under its family's key legend (families.<family>.keys, a trailing run of nulls trimmed). Fields: game_pk (key into games, whose entry is [date (local, from the feed's first play), opponent, home as 1/0]), ab, idx (event index in the plate appearance, -1 for a play-result decision; the decision id is game_pk:ab:idx), half (0 top, 1 bottom), inning, outs, base (three-bit code: 1 first, 2 second, 4 third), score_diff (the deciding club's lead before the play), li (MLB feed leverage index; null on the leadoff plate appearance), kind (index into kinds; absent when it equals the family), in_id / out_id / pitcher_id / due_id / ondeck_id (the names table keys them; a row carries ids only), slot, pos, mwpa (wins, realized value, not skill: the window's endpoint difference in win probability, sign to the deciding club), dvs (wins above the matched-state league baseline; null in a thin cell), flags (indexes into flags), window (the plays governed, each [event index into events, wp_after] or [event, wp_after, wp_before] where the feed's chain breaks, the first play always carrying wp_before, wp in percentage points; the play's ab is the row's ab plus its offset; win_len is the window's length, 0 for a counted family and for the steal, which happens between plays). Family extras ride beside: pitch_count and tto of the removed pitcher, inherited runners and inherited_scored (derived), first_pa_mwpa, walk_only_mwpa, the steal's model dv / er / realized_delta (its mwpa is that realized_delta, the steal itself, and it has no dvs), the bunt's league dv_cell beside its realized figure.
shards.storage_note: tracked in git by owner decision (spec 14.1, taken 2026-09-23 on the measured size): the shards are written to data/mgmt_decisions/ (schema 2, compacted to about 41 MB over 240) and committed with the board, so the box serves them before its first nightly

team_style.why_no_plus_metric: the gate battery found a club's decision value in this family does not repeat between halves of a season, so a plus metric on it would be a ranking of noise. The leverage board withholds its own for the same reason.

manager_attribution.why: the module stops at the attempt. A team-season is an UPPER BOUND on a manager (managers change, teams do not) and carries no repeatable signal in this family, so a manager entity would attribute a signal that is not there.

sacrifice_bunt.sentence: Sacrifice bunts cost the league 129 wins over 6,937 bunts in 8 seasons, 0.0186 wins each. All 3 positive cells are squeezes (runner on third, one out); best 3B at +0.0234 wins a bunt.

independent_control.source: StatsAPI wp_home_before / wpa_home, converted to the batting team's frame and divided by 100 (those columns are percentage points, not probabilities)
independent_control.why_it_is_not_the_metric: it is the REALIZED win-probability change of the plays that happened, so it carries outcome variance the decision did not choose. It is here to check the sign and the size of the modelled number against a win-expectancy model this repo did not build.

sacrifice_bunt.the_selection_problem: NOT SOLVED, STATED. Managers bunt with the batters they least want swinging, so E[WE | bunt] is measured over a weaker population than E[WE | swing]. This prices THE BUNT AS DEPLOYED, which is a fair read of what the league's bunting has been worth, and it is biased against the bunt as a tactic. Removing the bias needs a per-batter plate appearance model (the plan's M-ENG-1), which does not exist yet.
sacrifice_bunt.why_no_plus_metric: None is published here, and it is not an oversight. The running-game battery found per-agent decision value does not repeat between halves of a season; nothing has shown this family behaves differently, so a per-club column would be a ranking of noise a reader could not recognise as one. It needs its own split-half before it can ship.
sacrifice_bunt.two_outs_excluded: With two down an out ends the half-inning, so its value comes from the measured half-inning-start table while the alternative comes from the smooth model. Those are two estimators with nothing calibrating them against each other, so their difference has no guaranteed sign. A two-out sacrifice is also nearly nonexistent.

bullpen_and_lineup.blocked_on: bullpen decision value and lineup value: the pitcher not used and the batter not lifted need the availability model (M-PIT-9) and the per-plate-appearance model (M-ENG-1); lineup optimality needs M-ENG-1 and the lineup chain (M-ENG-2)
bullpen_and_lineup.why: two decision families are measured: the running game (-0.69 wins to the league) and the sacrifice bunt (-129 wins), a 188-fold gap in size, so neither generalises to the rest. The bullpen call and the pinch hit have more room and have not been measured. The decision ledger carries REALIZED value for seven families, which is what happened after the decision and not the decision's value; the counterfactual for the bullpen call and the pinch hit has not been measured.

what_this_page_does_not_claim: that any manager is better than any other. The running game returned a bounded null: no club's decision value repeats between halves of its own season, and the battery would have detected 0.0005 wins per attempt. Hence no plus metric on this page.
